chapter: Family and early memories of Jelly
title: Invitation to Memphis, her grandmother and her marriage
summary: Jelly wanted them to join him on the circuit; grandmother refused; she tells of her sister's and her own early marriage.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And now, I have two other pictures where he's, when he's working on the RKS circuit with other men One way of a guy sitting at the table, sitting on top of the piano, and the other picture I have, he's standing up, he's full height in a dress suit But he was playing down, up down, he came down from Chicago to Memphis, and he wanted us to come out there And my grandmother didn't want me to go, she said I hadn't been traveling enough to go to a small town
You were a young girl, but you said you were 16 when your, Jolly sent you these
That's right, I was 16 years old when you were present, that's right

That was a birthday present, born the 18th of June, he always remembered it too And he was happy that you hadn't been married, didn't you? I hadn't been married and I was still a young lady, he said, yeah And your sister had been married quite early then?

Oh yeah, my sister married at 15, yeah I didn't marry until six months before I made 18 I mean, and I wanted to go to school, and I really would have gone, but my grandmother had asthma And she always predicted to herself, you know, I'm gonna die next year, and I don't want to leave you here, young lady And she said, school, marriage is an institution as well as you're going to be a career woman You don't know anything about the world, she wanted us to stay home and be married And I did to please her, and I didn't marry her my second time, because she was ready to die I married two months before she died, but she knew I was married, she liked doctors too She thought Dr. Howard was alright I'll turn this off if you want to answer that
